author: Claude (autonomous PI, second host)
stage: stage 9 -- if one channel carries the harm, can a per-channel ceiling keep the rest of the envelope?
written_after: stage 7 TRAINING telemetry only (curriculum_comparison_ne128_20260828_055416.json). No stage-7 or stage-8 EVALUATION result existed when this was written, so every evaluation endpoint below is outcome-blind.

harm_is_one_channel.reading: Latency alone costs 2.7x what the other five channels cost together, in 3 of 3 seeds, and reaches 89% of the full envelope's damage. Losses are sub-additive (2.46 + 6.71 > 7.57), so there is mild interaction, but the ordering is not in doubt.

the_gap_cannot_see_it.reading: The most damaging channel raises the latent command-execution gap barely above the no-DR control -- below it in seed 8601 -- while the least damaging channels raise it most. The direction holds in 2 of 3 seeds and the per-seed gap estimates are visibly noisy, so this is recorded as 'the gap does not rank channels by harm', NOT as an anti-correlation. It is still enough to explain why gap-gating never protected the policy: the controller's only evidence is near-blind to the dominant harm channel.

absolute_thresholds_do_not_port.observed: the same absolute return floor (8.0) tripped 12/7/7 times here against 3-7 on the first host, driving terminal lambda to 0.339 against 0.4-0.6, purely because this host's reward level runs ~15% lower.
absolute_thresholds_do_not_port.reading: independent confirmation of the defect the relative guard was built to fix, and the same defect that makes stage 7's own H_L3 thresholds untransferable.

design.origin: the same settled step-24 origin as stages 7 and 8 (sha256 2fcb299a659c9cb2...)

arms.lucid_latcap_s4_rg: latency capped at 0.5 of its envelope, 4 intensity strata, relative guard, no anchor
arms.ta_lucid_50_latcap_s4_rg: the same plus a 50% target anchor

design.matched_uncapped_pair: stage 8's lucid_s4_rg and ta_lucid_50_s4_rg -- same seeds, same origin, everything but the cap. The design is a 2x2 over {cap, no cap} x {anchor, no anchor}.
design.why_cap_0_5_and_not_a_tuned_value: 0.5 is the midpoint of the configured 0-40 ms envelope, fixed before any evaluation was seen and not swept. It halves the one channel stage 7 identified as dominant while leaving the other five at full support. The cap is never graded on its own turf: every evaluation preset (dr_full at 40 ms, latency_60ms at 60 ms) tests latency OUTSIDE the capped training range, so a capped arm can only win by generalising past what it trained on.

evaluation.co_primary: latency_60ms success -- the cap's hardest case, 3x its training ceiling

hypotheses.H_C1: capping helps overall: ta_lucid_50_latcap_s4_rg beats ta_lucid_50_s4_rg on profile AUC by >= 2 pts.
hypotheses.H_C2: the cap buys retention: it beats its uncapped pair on id_clean by >= 5 pts.
hypotheses.H_C3: the cap does NOT cost out-of-range latency robustness: on latency_60ms it is within 3 pts of its uncapped pair. Losing more than that means the cap trades deployment latency margin for clean capability, and it is reported as a trade, not a win.
hypotheses.H_C4: the effect is about the channel, not the anchor: the capped-minus-uncapped gain on profile AUC has the same sign with and without the anchor.

decision_rules.seed_agreement: any directional claim must hold in >= 2 of 3 seeds
decision_rules.if_H_C3_fails: report and quantify the trade; never present AUC gains without the latency cost beside them.
decision_rules.cap_value_is_not_swept: 0.5 is the only cap run. If it wins it is one point, not a tuned optimum, and the paper says so.

not_yet_verified: all evaluation endpoints; written before any stage-7/8 evaluation existed
